background: L3 runtime closure for TP-DMX-PR1304-RED-LANE-PATH-REGEX-HARDENING-002. Automated review on this packet's own prior test-only draft (PR #1325) found and this session independently reproduced a live bypass: RedLaneScanner silently failed to block exact-match FORBIDDEN_PATHS entries carrying a control character. Adds an unconditional scanner-side short-circuit mirroring the hook's, plus a regression matrix covering exact-match, wildcard, exemption-spoof, arbitrary-malformed, and clean-control cases. Round 2 fixed a mutation-test methodology flaw (parametrized so all 13 probes are independently verified), pinned the donor content digest, tightened S1's HEAD-verification wording, and corrected the packet header's authority fields. Round 3 fixed three further findings: the filesystem-access test now mocks and asserts os.path.exists/open are never called (independently proven non-vacuous by the auditor moving the short-circuit and confirming the test then fails); S1 now asserts hard equality with origin/main after an explicit fast-forward, not mere ancestry (which silently tolerated a stale HEAD); and MUTATION_EVIDENCE.md's claim was corrected to distinguish the 7 probes that genuinely revert to a full silent bypass (Status.UNKNOWN, zero findings) from the 6 wildcard/exemption probes that only lose their MALFORMED_PATH_CONTROL_CHARACTER category label while remaining correctly Status.BLOCKED via PR #1322's independent red_lane_rules.py fix. red_lane_scanner.py is unchanged since round 1 across all three rounds. src/dopemux/dcp/red_lane_rules.py and .claude/hooks/dcp_surface_guard.py are untouched throughout, per packet scope. This PR does not merge as part of this proof.
